output.summary: KEP-4858 proposes tightening Kubernetes API validation of IP and CIDR string fields in core types, since the existing validation accepts ambiguous strings that net.ParseIP/ParseCIDR allow. It is implementable at stage beta, with implemented from 2026-02-09 per the status history.
output.rationale: Kubernetes validation of IP/CIDR fields accepts any string that net.ParseIP and net.ParseCIDR accept, and some of those strings are ambiguous and can cause security problems (CVE-2021-29923 is cited). Stricter validation was deferred so existing objects would not be invalidated, so the KEP sets a plan to tighten it behind a feature gate, with warnings first and without forcing fixes on unrelated updates. The source gives the motivation; the status history does not explain the reason for the change in stage.

alternatives.option: Update netutils.ParseIPSloppy and ParseCIDRSloppy as part of this KEP
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal: "There is a separate plan for this."

alternatives.option: Make immutable fields fixable when they are invalid
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal: "there was not a consensus that it was a good idea _in general_"

alternatives.option: Require canonical IPv6 form in legacy fields
alternatives.why_not: Non-goal because "we decided against that"; legacy non-canonical values would need forcible fix-up, and only warnings are added for them.

alternatives.option: Add cluster-level warnings or events for invalid IP/CIDR values in old objects
alternatives.why_not: Originally a goal but not implemented; listed as a non-goal.

evidence.quote: accepting any string accepted by the underlying functions (`net.ParseIP` and `net.ParseCIDR`) even though in some cases these strings had ambiguous meanings that could lead to security problems
we didn't want to retroactively invalidate existing API objects. This KEP sets forth the plan for finally moving forward on that.
Don't require pre-existing invalid fields to be fixed on unrelated updates.
This will initially be behind a feature gate.
Before that, do a few releases where IP/CIDR values that would be invalid according to the new rules cause apiserver warnings.
